name: Pharyngeal-Cervical-Brachial Variant of Guillain-Barré Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed diagnostic criteria for pharyngeal-cervical-brachial variant of Guillain-Barré syndrome

criteria.description: Acute onset of weakness predominantly affecting the oropharyngeal, neck, and upper limb muscles
Areflexia or hyporeflexia in the upper limbs
Minimal or no lower limb weakness at presentation
Presence of anti-GQ1b IgG antibodies in serum
Nerve conduction studies showing axonal neuropathy or demyelination predominantly in upper limbs

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of acute pharyngeal-cervical-brachial weakness with areflexia/hyporeflexia in upper limbs and minimal or no lower limb involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Anti-GQ1b antibodies support diagnosis but are not mandatory; nerve conduction studies aid confirmation.

searchTerms: acute mouth and throat muscle weakness

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral upper limb proximal muscle weakness
searchTerms: weakness in upper arm muscles on both sides

pathognomonic.symptomName: Areflexia or hyporeflexia in upper limbs
searchTerms: low or missing arm tendon reflexes
slurred speech from throat muscle weakness
speech problems due to bulbar muscle issues
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

occasional.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction (e.g., tachycardia, blood pressure fluctuations)
searchTerms: heart rate and blood pressure swings

rare.symptomName: Severe respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation
Cranial nerve III, IV, or VI palsies
searchTerms: drooping eyelid or eye muscle weakness
unpleasant sensory symptoms in upper limbs

laboratory: Presence of anti-GQ1b IgG antibodies in serum
Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein with normal cell count (albuminocytologic dissociation)
imaging: MRI of brain and cervical spine typically normal or nonspecific
Nerve conduction studies showing axonal neuropathy or demyelination predominantly in upper limbs
other: Electromyography demonstrating reduced motor unit potentials in affected muscles

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of descending paralysis starting with cranial nerves
History of ingestion or wound contamination
Fluctuating muscle weakness worsening with activity
MRI showing ischemic lesion in brainstem

redFlags: Rapid progression of bulbar weakness with respiratory compromise
Development of respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation
Signs of autonomic instability such as severe blood pressure fluctuations or arrhythmias
references: Ropper AH. The Guillain-Barré syndrome. N Engl J Med. 1992;326(17):1130-1136.
Wakerley BR, Uncini A, Yuki N. Guillain-Barré and Miller Fisher syndromes—new diagnostic classification. Nat Rev Neurol. 2014;10(9):537-544.
